transcript.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Our invoice lists “Embeddings, Aug 3-9” twice. Last time, support told us duplicates can’t be credited here and have to go through Finance, but can you credit the duplicate? Org copperleaf-ai.

queries: Support console duplicate-charge credits confirmed duplicate same request IDs credit limit Support may credit
current billing routing duplicate charge confirmed duplicate lines invoice credit Finance limits
Support Console Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes current published policy

{"name": "invoice-charge-review", "steps": "Goal: decide from console facts and current policy whether Support credits the line itself, opens a dispute and hands off, or only routes the request, then do it and tell the developer exactly what happened.

1. Identify. You need the org/account and the invoice (id or month). If missing, call ask_developer once with what is missing, e.g. ["org_id", "invoice_id", "invoice_month", "line_items", "request_ids"]. Don't ask for what they already wrote.
2. Look up. lookup_account (org or id). Note billing_channel, plan, payment_method, contracts. If the invoice id is unknown, pick it from the account's invoices by period; if several fit, ask.
3. Read the invoice. get_invoice. Look at duplicate_analysis:
   - Lines billing the identical request ids = console-confirmed duplicate. The later line is the duplicated one.
   - Same amount or description with different request ids = not a confirmed duplicate. Say so plainly, give each line's request id and amount, and don't credit.
   - Check already_credited and existing disputes so you don't act twice.
4. Get the policy. search_knowledge, e.g. ["support console duplicate charge credit dispute", "billing adjustments approval matrix support limit per line", plus the developer's situation]. Find the current published/final page that says what Support may credit and the limit, and the routing page for anything else. Ignore archived help articles and draft proposals for the rule (mention them only if the developer cites them). Note the chunk_id of the passage stating the limit.
5. Decide (from the passages, not memory):
   - Not a direct Redwood invoice (marketplace or reseller billing): Support issues nothing; tell them who bills and handles it, per the policy.
   - Confirmed duplicate within Support's limit: one credit note for the whole duplicated line, reason duplicate.
   - Confirmed duplicate over the limit: no credit; open a dispute on the duplicated line (reason duplicate_charge, its request ids), then escalate to the team the policy names with invoice, line and dispute id.
   - Not confirmed, or the developer says billed in error, or wants goodwill / an exception / removal of a correct charge: no credit; route per the routing table (load billing-handoff).
6. Confirm. confirm_with_developer with the exact action: "Issue a credit note of $X on invoice I line L (duplicate of line K, same request id R)" or "Open a dispute on I line L and hand it to <team>". If no: don't act; explain the alternative.
7. Act. issue_credit_note with policy_chunk_id and policy_limit_cents from step 4; or open_dispute then escalate_case with dispute_id and full details. If a hook blocks, read why and follow that path; never retry a failed write blindly.
8. Reply. Say what the console showed (lines, request ids, amounts), what you did (credit note id and amount / dispute id and team), and what happens next without promising an outcome or date. If they ask when a refund lands, answer only from a current source; otherwise say the team confirms it."}

Collect the intake details and hand the case to Billing Ops as the routing page describes. |"}, {"chunk_id": "f5b3760de72f9fac", "source": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-billing-credits-and-disputes", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes", "status": "published", "updated": "2026-02-05", "section": "body > Duplicate charges: what Support may credit | body > What Support never credits | body > Telling the customer", "text": "[body > Duplicate charges: what Support may credit]
Support's limit is set by Finance in the Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix (Finance shared drive) (the duplicate-charge credit row). It is per duplicated line and applies to the line's full amount. Don't split a larger duplicate into several smaller credits.

[body > What Support never credits]
- Goodwill, exceptions, SLA credits, or any credit someone says a manager, sales rep or Redwood engineer already approved. These stay with Finance, per the #support guidance from FP&A. Route the request; don't issue anything from the console.
- Marketplace purchases, which are billed by the marketplace.

[body > Telling the customer]
- Say what you did: the credit note and its amount, or that a dispute is open and Billing Ops has the case. Don't promise the outcome of a dispute or a date.

The support console can look up a customer's billing account, issue a credit note against invoice lines, and open a billing dispute. This page defines when Support uses each one. It amends the billing routing page for duplicate charges only; everything else on that page still applies.

[body > Look up the account first]
- Look up the customer's billing account in the console before you quote an amount, a plan, an invoice line, or whether a charge is a duplicate. You can find the account by its account id or by the customer's org name; ask for one of them if the customer hasn't given either.
- Quote amounts as the console shows them. Don't restate a figure the customer gives you as fact.

[body > Refund timing]
Refunds reach your card within 5-10 business days."}, {"chunk_id": "36d46119ce7a0647", "source": "google_drive/shared_drives/finance/billing-adjustments-approval-matrix", "title": "Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix", "status": "final", "updated": "2026-02-03", "section": "content > Approval matrix", "text": "[content > Approval matrix]
| Adjustment | Who issues it | Limit and approver |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate-charge credit (console-confirmed duplicate line on a direct invoice) | Support, from the support console | Up to $500 per duplicated line. Over that, Support opens a dispute and Billing Ops takes it |
| Billing-error correction other than a duplicate (wrong rate, quantity or product) | Billing Ops | Up to $2,000 per invoice; above that, the Controller |
| Refund of a paid invoice line after an approved adjustment | Billing Ops | Up to $5,000; above that, the Controller |
| Goodwill credit, waiver, or exception to a billing rule | Finance (FP&A) | Any amount, decided in FP&A's review. Support and Billing Ops route these requests and never issue them |
| SLA credit on a self-serve account | Finance (FP&A) | Self-serve plans carry no SLA. FP&A reviews any request as goodwill |"}, {"chunk_id": "e8c54d779d4c943a", "source": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/reseller-billed-invoice-disputes-2026", "title": "Reseller-Billed Invoices: Disputes and Credits", "status": "published", "updated": "2026-04-02", "section": "body > Scope | body > What Support does | body > Partnerships limits", "text": "[body > Scope]
Customers who buy Redwood through a reseller receive the reseller's invoice, not Redwood's. This page covers disputes and credits on those invoices only. It is not the procedure for duplicate charges on a direct Redwood invoice; for those, use the support console credits and disputes page.

[body > What Support does]
- Confirm in the console that the account is reseller-billed. A direct Redwood invoice in the console means this page does not apply.
- Point the customer to their reseller, who raises the dispute with Partnerships.
- Support issues no credit note and opens no dispute for a reseller-billed account: the reseller's invoice isn't in the console.

[body > Partnerships limits]
Partnerships may credit a reseller up to $2,500 per invoice under the partner agreement. That limit has nothing to do with Support's own limits.
